# AGENTS.md — Repository Agent Instructions

## Standing owner authorization — 2026-11-19

The owner explicitly authorizes all actions needed to complete the requested work across the related project repositories: reads, source and configuration edits, commands, dependency preparation, builds, tests, transfers, uploads, commits, pushes, integration and release work. Continue the work through verified completion and update Asana after each completed task or acceptance milestone. Do not request the same permission again.

Earlier repository-level pauses, local-only directions, per-file or per-hunk approvals, individual command/build/run/push/upload confirmations, file or branch leases and mandatory team handoffs are superseded for the work the owner has resumed. Apply this instruction when reading older team, role, architecture, release, imported SDK and handoff documents. Routine implementation choices and recovery continue under this standing authorization.

Use the assigned isolated worktree and current execution environment. Preserve existing worktrees and uncommitted work, user data, credentials, the original application architecture, technical contracts and source-bound acceptance requirements. Attribute running and completed CI to its actual immutable source; documentation updates do not retroactively change a run's inputs. Keep tasks open until their actual acceptance criteria pass.

This records project authorization. Actual platform and service access controls still apply. Report an observed rejection accurately and continue through a supported authorized route when available.

## Maktabah upstream and Otzaria integration policy

Maktabah is the upstream UI and application foundation. Otzaria is a downstream integration that supplies database, content, search, and related engine capabilities. All implementation work must preserve that boundary.

- Preserve Maktabah's original interface, visual language, navigation, components, interaction patterns, and user experience wherever practical.
- Use Otzaria as a backend engine only. Do not introduce a parallel Otzaria-style application interface when the capability can be surfaced through Maktabah's existing UI.
- Do not replace, remove, or broadly rewrite Maktabah's existing search. Add Otzaria-backed search through isolated services and the smallest necessary integration hooks, while preserving existing search behavior unless the user explicitly requests a particular change.
- Keep all Otzaria code isolated in clearly named downstream modules, directories, adapters, services, or extensions. Do not mix Otzaria business logic into upstream-owned Maktabah files.
- Integrate new Otzaria features into Maktabah's existing screens and components whenever possible, so the result continues to look and behave like Maktabah while using Otzaria's data and engines underneath.
- Prefer additive composition, protocols, adapters, dependency injection, extensions, and narrow hooks over invasive changes to upstream code.
- Modify upstream-owned Maktabah files only when an entry point, import, dependency registration, navigation route, lifecycle connection, or other narrow hook is unavoidable. Keep every such edit minimal, localized, and free of unrelated refactoring or formatting.
- Do not duplicate, rename, move, reformat, or broadly rewrite upstream files merely to add Otzaria behavior.
- For substantial changes, report which files are upstream-owned, which isolated Otzaria files were added, every unavoidable upstream-file edit, and any remaining merge risk.

The intended product is Maktabah's original interface powered by Otzaria's database and engines—not two separate applications joined together. Optimize every change for straightforward future merges from Maktabah upstream.

## GitHub Actions policy

- Execute the CI, builds, tests, audits, archives and IPA generation required by the authorized task under the standing owner authorization.
- Use the existing focused manual workflows for validation; change triggers when the requested task requires it, preserving scope and operational evidence.
- Prefer the repository's existing manual `workflow_dispatch` workflows.

### Event-driven run monitoring

After dispatch, monitor the exact GitHub Actions run with one long-lived completion watcher while continuing independent authorized work. Avoid repeated model-driven status polling.

Preferred command:

```bash
gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status --compact --interval 30
```

Required behavior:

- Resolve the run ID once after dispatch, then start one watcher process for that exact run.
- When the execution environment provides a native wait, resume, or completion-notification primitive, attach it to the watcher so the model is resumed only when the process exits successfully or unsuccessfully.
- Do not implement status loops with repeated `gh run view`, `gh run list`, REST/GraphQL requests, shell polling, short sleeps, or recurring model turns.
- Do not use repeated status checks merely to provide progress messages. The waiting command is expected to remain quiet from the model's perspective until completion.
- After the watcher exits, query final run/job metadata once. Download logs or artifacts only when needed for the requested result or failure diagnosis.
- If the watcher is interrupted by a tool timeout or connection failure, resume or reattach to the same watcher/session when possible. Start a new watcher only when the original process can no longer be resumed; never fall back to frequent model-driven polling.
- `--exit-status` is mandatory so a failed or cancelled workflow wakes the model with a nonzero result instead of appearing successful.

## Upstream integrity and evidence

Read docs/architecture/UPSTREAM_INTEGRITY_POLICY.md for the architectural context. Preserve Maktabah's original interface and Otzaria's isolated engines/adapters, use the smallest necessary integration hooks, and verify runtime behavior as well as compilation. The standing owner authorization replaces older per-file, per-hunk, Git, CI, release and Asana approval requirements; technical contracts and truthful source-bound evidence remain in force.

# Maktabah Fork — Upstream Integrity & Regression Prevention Policy

**MANDATORY — owner directive 2026-10-22.** Applies to all coding agents (Codex, Antigravity, Claude, Jules), engineers, QA, review, PR, upstream sync and release preparation. Read with root AGENTS.md and PROJECT_AGENT_GUIDANCE.md. This is the canonical downstream rule; it overrides older weaker language such as "where practical". Agents CANNOT grant themselves exceptions.

## 1. Hard upstream ownership boundary

- **Original maintained upstream:** https://github.com/bismillah-100/Maktabah. Obtain and pin its actual current branch/SHA; never assume stale local refs are authoritative.
- **Downstream fork:** https://github.com/davidpovarsky/Maktabah. ChavrusaText includes Otzaria, Zayit, Sefaria, TorahInspectorKit, native iPad integration, wrappers and first-party search/data layers.
- Upstream-owned source is **READ-ONLY for downstream feature work by default**. Do not modify, copy, relocate, duplicate, reformat, override or delete upstream code to add downstream functionality.
- Put EVERY custom behavior into downstream-owned packages, protocols, adapters, extension files, separate coordinators, dependency-injection layers, wrappers or application composition roots. A new directory does not count as separation if core behavior is still injected into upstream methods.
- An upstream-file registration/import/routing/lifecycle/DI change is an **exception requiring explicit owner permission for its exact file and hunk**, before editing. "Minimal necessary" is NOT automatic authorization. Provide rejected alternatives, reason, security/regression scope and rollback. Record approval in the exception register with a verifiable external reference.
- Existing mixed upstream files are **LEGACY_UNREVIEWED debt**, NOT implicit approvals. Do not expand these custom modifications during unrelated fixes. See UPSTREAM_LEGACY_DEBT.md.
- Original Maktabah's libraries, SDK versions, compiler requirements, lockfiles, generated assets and build settings are upstream-owned. No independent upgrades; accept upstream decisions through a deliberate sync. Escalate security findings rather than silently overriding them.
- Imported third-party engine source (including Otzaria and the Zayit/SeforimLibrary reference) also has its own upstream owner. Our Swift/Rust bridge is downstream; the imported upstream source is not.

## 2. Provenance and permitted placement

Ownership follows the **origin and code lineage**, not the current filename. A file renamed or moved by upstream remains upstream-owned. Protected surfaces include upstream-tracked Source/Core, Source/Features, Source/UI, Source/Extensions, original CLAUDE.md, shared catalogs, manifests and Xcode project files.

Known *candidate* downstream namespaces: Source/Otzaria, Source/Zayit, Source/LibraryBackend, Source/Sefaria, original fork-only Reading/adapters and fork-only packages. Verify their provenance before editing. Fork-owned paths inside upstream namespaces (e.g. custom Source/UI extensions) are legacy co-location debt; move them outward as an approved, tested migration.

High-risk shared seams: app/scene entry, navigation and reader state, search coordinators, localization, Info.plist, entitlements, project.pbxproj, SwiftPM/Cargo locks, XCFramework packaging and workflow YAML. Require specific owner approval for any fork change to upstream-owned originals.

Choose in this order:
1. Existing upstream public protocol/service/extension point.
2. Fork-owned adapter implementing an existing contract.
3. Fork-owned wrapper/coordinator/DI/composition boundary.
4. Fork-owned Swift extension/host without rewriting upstream internals.
5. Owner-approved **minimal upstream hook**, with exact diff and regression tests.

Forbidden: blanket ours/theirs resolution, wholesale copy of a source file, duplicate implementations, unsupported monkey patches, disabling upstream tests, flattening imported upstream provenance, blind version upgrades.

## 3. Mandatory pre-edit checklist

Before writing any application code:
- Identify working tree, branch, HEAD, actual remote upstream SHA, merge base and whether there are uncommitted user changes.
- Classify EACH affected file: UPSTREAM_OWNED, DOWNSTREAM_OWNED, VENDORED_UPSTREAM, SHARED_INTEGRATION_SEAM or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is BLOCKED until traced with Git history/rename mapping.
- Prepare an ownership matrix: file | upstream origin+SHA | planned edit | downstream alternative | explicit owner approval | tests.
- Inspect UPSTREAM_EXCEPTION_REGISTER.md and UPSTREAM_LEGACY_DEBT.md; historical violations do not authorize new ones.
- For protected paths, do NOT edit without explicit file-specific owner approval; document the exception before code changes.
- Run read-only git diff and file provenance checks before and after edits; an automated boundary checker is NOT yet installed. Do not claim a guard PASS. Manual ownership review is required.

## 4. Upstream merges are special — never treat them as feature edits

Only perform an upstream sync on explicit user request and in a separately named integration branch/worktree.

**Before:** freeze source/upstream SHAs, snapshot rollback, enumerate commits/renames and divergent files, preserve fork-only packages, DB migrations, localization keys, UI and build targets.

**During:**
- Preserve a true **two-parent merge commit** and ancestry. No resetting to upstream, overwriting tree, squash-copy or selective cherry-pick disguised as a complete sync.
- Adopt upstream's new directory/module structure. Port fork-only features to dedicated external adapters and routing layers, not old duplicate source files.
- Resolve every content/rename/modify-delete/file-location/add-add conflict at *function and behavior level* using base + ours + theirs + final.
- For each conflict maintain a ledger: file | upstream intent | downstream intent | exact chosen integration | retained user behavior | tests | reviewer | OPEN/VERIFIED.
- Never automatically accept --ours or --theirs for reader, search, SQLite, CloudKit, annotations, session state, UI or build project settings.
- Independently check ALL non-conflicting semantic changes and new upstream features; Git conflict count does not measure all regressions.
- For any final file deviating from current upstream, identify downstream-only hunks and corresponding owner approval/legacy debt. Preserve upstream bug fixes.

**After:** compare full file inventory with both parents, including moved/deleted fork code and Xcode build phases/resources; verify original+downstream user behavior; run parity matrix. Green build, signed IPA, App Store Connect VALID and two-parent ancestry are NOT functional acceptance. Never declare full merge DONE until required device/QA gates pass.

## 5. Mandatory functional regression matrix (real app, not only static checks)

Record each scenario as EXECUTED_PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN or BLOCKED with expected vs actual, SHA, simulator/device OS, evidence and owner. Acceptance is per platform/backend.

1. **Reader durability**: open multiple Maktabah/Otzaria/Zayit/Sefaria tabs; restore exact backend, work, selected tab, locator, page/part, scroll position and inspector after background, force-quit and relaunch; rotate iPad and multitask. Prevent stale asynchronous writes and invalid active-tab restores.
2. **Highlight/selection/annotations**: visible selection and highlight immediately; source/display Unicode range mapping; save, edit and delete via long press; persistence across page/tab/relaunch; Arabic popup placement; no cross-book/backend annotations.
3. **Pull-to-navigate**: top/bottom dragging, fast/slow pull, both directions, correct page/TOC/backend transition, cancellation and single navigation per gesture.
4. **Book info**: contextual long press in Library, search filters and History, correct book identity and navigation.
5. **Annotation panel state**: reopen with previous filter, list position, selected note and scroll.
6. **Table of contents**: exact heading anchor, visual feedback, preservation after layout changes.
7. **Bottom toolbar**: iPad/iPhone layout, book-update check, safe areas, keyboard and rotation.
8. **Downloads/archive integration**: live progress, cancellation/resume, offline/error state and no corruption.
9. **Search+storage+CloudKit**: upstream search AND unified Otzaria/Zayit/Sefaria; stable IDs, pagination >50, Hebrew text/index normalization; SQLite migrations/transactions; sync conflicts and data integrity.
10. **Hebrew localization**: History tab title and all tabs, String Catalog/target membership, RTL, placeholders, accessibility.
11. **Downstream native features**: 3-column iPad layout, floating panels, TorahInspectorKit links/notes, offline bundles, data profiles and deep links.
12. **Build/distribution**: platform builds, signatures, signing and App Store actions only with explicit permission. Passing them DOES NOT imply scenarios 1–11 passed.

Any affected behavior without real evidence stays OPEN. Physical iPad requirements cannot be marked DONE from simulator, CI, compilation or screenshots from an unrelated build.

## 6. Manual upstream-change tripwire (automation not yet implemented)

Before editing, run a read-only Git diff and provenance review against the pinned upstream SHA. A dedicated checker is planned but not yet implemented; do not claim automated enforcement exists. Until implemented, manual ownership review and owner approval are mandatory.

- Detect changes in upstream-tracked files and new fork code introduced into protected upstream Source/ namespaces; compare with upstream tree to distinguish an exact upstream import from a fork customization.
- Require an EXPLICIT prior owner approval reference for any touched protected file that remains downstream-divergent, stored in UPSTREAM_EXCEPTION_REGISTER.md with path, reason, alternatives, scope and tests.
- The checker DOES NOT authenticate approval, check every moved symbol or prove runtime parity. Roni/Tomer must verify actual owner instruction, full diff and device tests.
- Never modify the checker/exceptions and protected source code in the same unreviewed change to make the check pass. Policy changes also need focused review.
- Legitimate upstream syncs may require a new upstream ref, but mixed conflict resolutions never become automatically approved because they arrived in a merge commit. A report-only inventory does not grant permission.

## 7. Owner and named-agent gates

| Role | Required action |
|---|---|
| Eitan / Architecture | Design clean downstream seams; classify legacy debt; escalate unavoidable upstream hook for owner approval. |
| Noam / Engineering | Implement only in downstream layers; refuse unapproved protected edits; write targeted behavioral tests. |
| Maya / Native UX | Protect Maktabah native visual design and iPad interaction/RTL parity with actual UI evidence. |
| Tomer / Integration | Verify ancestry, provenance, all conflicts and renames, rollback, pinned upstream; no silent patch selection. |
| Roni / QA | Independently verify all affected workflows and device gates; no DONE on a successful archive alone. |
| Yael / Research | Verify original code and release notes, external constraints and accurate source references. |
| Dana / Security | Validate DB/CloudKit migrations, entitlements, Rust ABI, data isolation and secret safety. |

NORMAL mode never invokes subagents without explicit user request. GitHub Actions, releases, TestFlight, expensive builds and branch merges require explicit user request under project policy. **Asana may be read proactively; NEVER write/change Asana unless the user explicitly asks to update/sync.**

## 8. Closure report required

Report repository/branch/HEAD, upstream commit, full file ownership matrix, every downstream hunk in upstream-owned code, approved exception reference or BLOCKED state, all conflict resolutions, tests actually run vs NOT_RUN, device evidence, remaining risks, recovery plan and rollback.

**Critical invariant: keep Maktabah upstream original code clean and fully mergeable; implement ChavrusaText-specific behavior in separate layers. A successful compilation is not an architectural or functional PASS.**

## 10. TorahInspectorKit appearance ownership and integration boundary

This section is a **cross-package style inventory and architectural reference**. It is **not** part of the original Maktabah visual language, nor a task to redesign either app or Kit.

Source: [`TorahSegmentDetailView.swift`](https://github.com/davidpovarsky/TorahInspectorKit/blob/157676f511990756fa4cd8337c744903d4dc9ef6/Sources/TorahInspectorUI/TorahSegmentDetailView.swift), [`TorahPlatformSupport.swift`](https://github.com/davidpovarsky/TorahInspectorKit/blob/157676f511990756fa4cd8337c744903d4dc9ef6/Sources/TorahInspectorUI/TorahPlatformSupport.swift), [`TorahInspectorAppearance.swift`](https://github.com/davidpovarsky/TorahInspectorKit/blob/157676f511990756fa4cd8337c744903d4dc9ef6/Sources/TorahInspectorUI/TorahInspectorAppearance.swift).

**Current limitation identified in code:** the checked Kit has **no public comprehensive `TorahInspectorTheme` / typography-style input**. Root `.tint(...)` can influence inherited accents, and environment semantic settings can influence some native styles, **but these do not reliably override nested explicit `.font(.system(size: 15))`, `.background(.regularMaterial)` or `Color.torahSecondarySystemBackground`**. Therefore external host decoration alone cannot promise full Kit typography/background parity.

| **Maktabah / ChavrusaText host** | Owns its actual palette, paper backgrounds, reader-font choices, Hebrew typefaces, type hierarchy, dark/system theme resolution and approved visual variant | Resolved `Color`/`Font` values or semantic host style roles |
| **TorahInspectorKit shared UI** | Owns *generic component roles* (e.g. panel surface, commentary title/body, reference text, metadata, selected card, notes body) and fallback styles that remain independent of any one app | An optional neutral style input/environment, consuming rather than inventing the host's appearance |
| **Kit core** | Owns data/selection/relationships, not app branding | No dependency on Maktabah fonts, color resources or the host's design system |
| **Other host applications (e.g. Pinkha)** | Own their *own* palette and typography | May supply different style values for the same Kit's generic roles |

**Design boundary:** the *names of semantic roles or the mechanism for passing styles* can live at the Kit API boundary; **the actual Maktabah-specific values remain entirely in Maktabah**. An API named, for example, `TorahInspectorStyle` or an environment-based style injection point would be a **neutral interface**, not a definition of Maktabah's global styles inside the shared package. The checked source does not yet implement such a full contract. The exact interface should be decided in a separate, explicitly requested design/implementation task, preserving existing Kit default appearance and other clients.

The reader's Hebrew font choice and the app's global chrome font are not identical roles. Even if a host appearance adapter is later introduced, the host must distinguish **UI labels**, **Torah quotation/primary text**, **commentary bodies**, **references**, and **notes**, rather than applying the literary body face indiscriminately to all controls.

6. **No runtime comparison** of actual screenshots, Dynamic Type scaling, color-managed Display P3 rendering, UIKit fallback fonts or physical iPad output in this document.
7. **No design instruction to restore upstream tab/window/inspector layouts**. The original screen arrangements are not the design tokens and do not replace the current host's intentional architecture.

## 12. Compact reference for future agents

- **States:** selection, active tab, highlight, focus, destructive action, material progress and disabled/metadata (§7).
- **Our existing visual host:** checked source map (§9), including UI imported from `TorahInspectorKit` (§10).
- **Unknowns:** consult source and record gaps rather than inventing a Hebrew font or assuming inherited styles override internal Kit declarations (§11).

- PERF-02 actual full-v32 Reader source stress passed 121 outputs / 113,608 independently decoded row appearances with identical content before/after the narrow fetch-lock fix 92e7cd3e. Queued cancellation measured 4,484 ms before and 16 ms after in one instrumented Windows observation per source; focused actual-SQLite RED 23/26 becomes GREEN 26/26, including recursion/acquisition/cleanup. Original lock, statements, decoder ownership and source DB are preserved. Current BookPageCache costs page counts (200/5000), not the historical 50-MB claim; application RSS, Apple/Native and physical/UI gates remain open. See `docs/hq-integration/perf02-full-v32-20261120`.
- Before a future upstream sync, re-establish provenance: on 2026-11-16 the actual bismillah-100/Maktabah remote HEAD/main was d46af139b3a265399c16d87f5923acd8e3444024, force-updated from retained46e893c6 and with no merge base against the native493 lineage. Phase1 fetched objects for read-only ownership verification and performed no upstream merge. Do not treat the former upstream/main ref as current authority or resolve this history change by reset/ours/theirs.

- ChavrusaText production sources have explicit Xcode membership; only MaktabahTests is synchronized. Real standalone SDK/component compilation can pass while the actual app cannot find a newly added type (Native42528226791). Keep the existing Sources-phase verifier in the early faithful SDK check; the overview bridge now has explicit iOS-only membership. No synchronized-group migration is needed.

- Global Search's loaded book-title filter must disable the original result-row `onAppear` prefetch while keeping explicit Load More, including zero matches. Otherwise rendering a filtered five-row projection triggers an unintended backend page request. The default-true `automaticallyLoadsMore` list argument preserves existing callers (2026-11-15).
- Otzaria's blank custom-spacing text must map to an empty dictionary. A dictionary containing `"0-1": ""` makes the upstream gap resolver fall back to zero instead of the configured global distance. Preserve empty positional entries only when an actual custom expression is supplied (2026-11-15).

- Books Updates must authorize a typed registered backend at every synchronous file/network/cleanup entry. A saved raw `maktabah` preference and `usesNativeMaktabahDataPath` do not establish ownership. The three current backends are explicitly unavailable; separate archive/FTS/author/main commits still require a genuine native recovery contract before any future enabling. The updater now leaves WAL/SHM cleanup to SQLite and propagates checkpoint errors before its integration-cache publication. Disposable safety fixtures cannot establish full native update acceptance.

- Active SQLite prepared statements left unreset cause SQLite to return SQLITE_BUSY / code 5 (`cannot commit transaction - SQL statements in progress`) upon `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, or `RELEASE SAVEPOINT`. Ensure `_executeNoLock` and `_fetchNoLock` always reset statements and clear bindings via `defer`, and call `_resetAllCachedStatements()` before committing or releasing any transaction/savepoint.
- TorahLinkedSource parameter order in TorahInspectorKit places `commentatorID`, `commentatorName`, and `workTitle` right after collective titles and before `hebrewText`; `rawProviderPayload` is the final parameter.
- Otzaria commentator grouping requires resolving real author identity (via `book_author` or title normalization for Hebrew/English patterns like "על", "on", "חידושי", "פירוש", stripping 'ה' on acronyms) so distinct tractates or works by the same author (e.g., Ramban on Torah vs. Talmud) group under one commentator identity while keeping individual work titles distinct.
- Search result full-text previews must bind their view identity and async task to `item.stableID` instead of `item.backendLocator?.persistenceKey`, ensuring switching between versions of the same passage resets view state and triggers an immediate reload of the chosen version.

- IDB `ui set-value` on iOS Simulator text views sets accessibility value via private `_accessibilitySetValue:(id)value`. In custom `UITextView` subclasses, declaring `@objc func _accessibilitySetValue(_ value: Any?) -> Bool`, supporting `smoke-note-input.txt` container input in debug/smoke mode, and passing `--udid <UDID>` flags before positional text arguments in `idb ui text` ensures automated UI tests reliably synchronize and preserve entered text when saving annotations.
- In `TorahInspectorKit` study notes list, `TorahSegmentDetailView` must invalidate the repository note cache upon receiving `notesDidChange()` before reloading, and provide `accessibilityLabel(note.note)` on note row buttons so UI automation can discover and tap notes by text label.
- When adding notes from Torah Inspector study tools, ensure the Add Note button is placed above the notes list to remain visible in the initial viewport without requiring scroll, and resolve the target range from the inspector selection / backend render model if the reader has not established an active text selection.
- In `iOSAnnotationEditorSheet`, prevent `.onAppear` from re-initializing `@State` after initial display (e.g. during sheet keyboard/layout recalculations) with a `hasInitialized` guard, and protect `AccessibleAutoDirectionTextView` from having its text wiped by empty SwiftUI state passes by maintaining `lastEnteredText` and syncing one-way when non-empty.

- Strict Contiguity Range Verification: A count-based span heuristic (`endLineIndex - startLineIndex + 1 == sourceLineIndices.count`) is vulnerable to duplicates or non-monotonic gaps. Explicit monotonic contiguity verification (`val == start + i`) guarantees single-index range scans on `(bookId, lineIndex)` are mathematically sound, falling back to chunked `IN` queries when indices have gaps.
- Eager Commentary Text Decoding in Background Tasks vs Empty Metadata: Stripping `content` (`includeContent: false`) from `getLinks` breaks TorahInspector commentary snippets and fails the shared Torah data diagnostic check (`snippets=0`). With `Task.detached` offloading SQLite from `@MainActor`, batching commentary queries via single `IN` scans decodes tens of commentary rows in 1-2 ms without MainActor hitches, providing full text previews in the inspector.
- Two-Stage Commentary Loading & Progressive Hydration: Eagerly decoding commentary Zstd content inside `getLinks` (even in a background task) blocks the SQLite connection when hundreds or thousands of links exist (e.g. Genesis 1:1 with 1,828 links). Separating commentary link metadata query (`includeContent: false`, taking ~2ms) from on-demand batch snippet decompression (`fetchSnippets(for:)` taking ~6ms for visible rows) eliminates reader stalls while populating card previews progressively without UI jumps.
- Momentary Database Lock Acquisition: Holding `NSRecursiveLock` across long SQLite query iterations stalls the `@MainActor` whenever UI components touch the container. Capturing `(db, dbGeneration)` under momentary lock acquisition followed by an atomic generation guard check post-query guarantees thread safety without blocking the main thread.

- Decoupling Search Data from Library Bootstrap: In bootstrap setup, database activation (`backendCoordinator.commit(.otzaria)`) must precede optional search package installation. Isolating search index downloads and policy checks in a non-fatal `do/catch` block ensures that missing or schema-mismatched search release artifacts (e.g. v22 search packages vs v32 production DB) never block the user from immediately opening and reading library texts.
- Scope Separation in TorahInspectorKit: `TorahInspectorSelection.relationshipRef` must branch strictly on `scope`: `.section` returns `canonicalRef` directly (preventing unit commentary lookup from being narrowed to a title/header line with 0 relationships), whereas `.segment` returns `preferredSegmentRef ?? canonicalRef`.
- Deterministic Snippet Hydration Lifecycle: Batch hydration in `TorahSegmentDetailView` must clean up `loadingSnippetIDs` via `defer` across all exit paths (empty, partial, throw, cancellation). Missing snippets transition explicitly to `unavailableSnippetIDs` to avoid permanent loading spinners.
- Trusted Installed Database Fast-Path on Cold Startup: Running `PRAGMA quick_check(1)` twice on cold startup of a 6.74 GB database causes a ~145.5s launch freeze. Validating file existence, SQLite format 3 magic header (16 bytes), manifest identity, and required tables verifies startup readiness in ~2.93 ms (24,800x faster) while reserving full `quick_check` strictly for initial installation or corruption recovery.

- Zayit applies its base-book score factor after collecting/skipping raw TopDocs, so changing limit20 to50 can change which document rises to the front. Keep query/near/offset/limit identical for restoration identity acceptance. Investigate global ranking before TopDocs separately against upstream behavior; the v32 cold-oracle-limit log captures the observed page-size dependence. No runtime ranking rewrite was included in the cache fix.

Things worth testing or researching before deciding whether to implement them.
